production.note: US model years 2022-2024. Start: Audi of America, 9 Feb 2021, 'Introducing the 2022 Audi e-tron GT and RS e-tron GT'. End year is provisional and rests on Kelley Blue Book (database): 2024 lists 'RS e-tron GT Sedan 4D', '590 HP' (kbb-rs-etron-gt-2024); 2025 lists only the 'RS e-tron GT Performance', '912 HP' (kbb-rs-etron-gt-2025), the updated car, which would be its own record.

body.note: Kelley Blue Book: 'RS e-tron GT Sedan 4D'; Audi calls it a 'grand turismo' (four-door).

configuration.note: Two permanently excited synchronous motors, one per axle: 'The RS e-tron GT shares its front motor with the entry e-tron GT but has a more powerful rear motor'.

drivetrain.note: 'the RS e-tron GT distributes up to 637 horsepower to all four wheels'

transmission.note: 'A unique feature in contrast to much of the Audi electric grand tourer's competition is its two-speed transmission' (on the rear axle; Cars.com lists '2-Speed A/T', carscom-rs-etron-gt-2022).

powerHp.note: Maximum rating with overboost, per the boost rule. Quote: "a net 590 horsepower and up to 637 horsepower with overboost". Ordinary rating 590 hp.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: spec databases. 2022 US RS e-tron GT, single configuration. Cars.com quote: "Base Curb Weight: 5,139 lbs". Kelley Blue Book (kbb-rs-etron-gt-2022): "Curb Weight 5137 pounds" (0.04% apart). No Audi of America or major magazine figure was found.

sources.title: The electric gran turismo: Introducing the 2022 Audi e-tron GT and RS e-tron GT

discrepancies.reason: Two databases differ by 2 lb (rounding or data entry).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 5,139 lb (Cars.com); the difference is negligible.

provisionalNote: Weight rests on Cars.com and Kelley Blue Book (databases, 5,139 / 5,137 lb); an Audi of America specification sheet or a major magazine's specification panel would replace it. The last pre-update US model year (2024) also rests on Kelley Blue Book; an Audi of America release on the 2025 update would replace it.
